source.title: Fluctuations, bias, variance and ensemble of learners: exact asymptotics for convex losses in high-dimension
source.authors: Bruno Loureiro; Cédric Gerbelot; Maria Refinetti; G. Sicuro; Florent Krzakala

page_placements.theme: Averaging and ensemble allocation alter interpolation peaks

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper develops an asymptotic analysis and numerical results for double-descent-like test-error behavior in random-feature models, rather than reproducing the original deep-network experiments.
record.gate_note: The authors discuss prior double-descent results by other researchers, which are not rows. Numerical results in Figures 2, 3, and 5 are reported as plotted averages; individual plotted values are not given in text. The paper also reports learner disagreement, recorded separately as a related finding rather than as a version of the claim.
record.test_reason: The paper derives exact high-dimensional asymptotics, checked by simulation, for test error of random-feature ridge and logistic learners and their ensembles as p/n varies. It reports an interpolation peak for single learners and decomposes it into a smooth fluctuation-free part and a fluctuation (variance) part. This is a different method (theory plus random-feature models) aimed at whether and why model-wise double descent occurs (V4) and what drives the peak (V6).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The main contribution is an exact asymptotic theory, proved via AMP, of ensembles of convex GLMs on correlated features. The authors conclude the interpolation peak comes from variance over the random weights: a fluctuation term that ensembling suppresses. This extends prior ridge results to logistic loss. They also find that score averaging beats majority vote and that overparameterization increases learner agreement.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes synthetic random-feature/generalized linear models in a high-dimensional limit and compares theory with numerical experiments; it does not reproduce the original deep-network model-size experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported curves vary with p/n and with ensemble size K. In ridge regression the fluctuation contribution also has a bump at p/n = d/n; in the logistic classification comparison, score averaging outperforms majority vote for K = 3.

fits_no_version.finding: The probability that two random-feature learners disagree decreases with overparameterization (Fig. 5 center).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Overparameterization increases agreement between independently trained random-feature learners.

fits_no_version.finding: Score averaging gives lower test error than majority vote at K=3; the two coincide as K→∞.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In random-feature logistic ensembles, averaging scores outperforms majority vote.

record.peer_reviewed: Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment
record.problems: The plotted numerical results are not reported as extractable numeric values in the text. Experiments are on synthetic random-feature models, and the paper does not test epochs, sample-count sweeps, or deep networks directly. No error bars or confidence intervals are reported.

untested.parts: Not tested: no deep networks are trained. Random features serve only as a proxy for the lazy regime.
Not tested: no sweep over epochs or training time.
Not tested: n/d is fixed at 2 and sample count is not swept.
Only random-feature GLMs (ridge and logistic, erf activation) at one n/d and near-zero λ are tested. No other model classes are tested.
Not tested: no effective-complexity measure predicting peak location.

Untested: label noise (targets are noiseless). Untested: whether optimally tuned regularization removes the peak (λ is held at 10^-4 or 10^-6). Multiple peaks appear only as a bump in the ridge fluctuation term.
Not tested: no re-expression against an effective parameter count.

missing.what: Analytic order parameters m, q0, q1 and the ratio q1/q0 for logistic loss, all showing a kink at the interpolation threshold.
Statement that the benefit of ensembling correlates with learner disagreement, which is largest at small p/n.

record.verdict_notes: The targets are noiseless, so the peak arises with no label noise, from random-feature variance alone. Regularization is held near zero and never tuned, so the regularization part of V6 is untested. The original sources do not include this paper. Figure values are not readable from the text, so states rest on the authors' statements and on Eqs. 10 and 14.

versions.untested_parts: The reported experiments and analysis use random-feature/generalized linear models, not deep networks tested across model size.
No sweep over training epochs or training time is reported.
No experiment varies training sample count near the interpolation threshold to measure whether more data raises test error.
The results concern random-feature models and specified synthetic settings, not all model classes or a general capacity sweep across model classes.
The paper does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count.

The paper attributes the double-descent contribution to fluctuations associated with random weights and reports a fluctuation decomposition. It does not experimentally vary label noise, test triple or multiple peaks, or show disappearance under optimally tuned regularization.
The paper does not re-express the curve against an effective parameter count to test whether the second descent becomes an ordinary U-shape.

relationships.condition: Single learners and finite-K ridge ensembles of random-feature models, near-zero λ, n/d=2
relationships.reason: Test error peaks or diverges at the interpolation threshold p=n and falls again beyond it. The divergence persists at every finite K for ridge (r1, r8–r13).
relationships.display_finding: Test error peaked or diverged at p=n and declined beyond it, with ridge divergence persisting for every finite ensemble size K.

relationships.condition: Ensembles of random-feature learners, increasing K up to K→∞
relationships.reason: The peak shrinks as K grows and vanishes at K→∞. There the logistic error is flat past threshold and the ridge error is smooth (r2–r5, r14).
relationships.display_finding: The peak shrank with K and vanished as K→∞, leaving logistic error flat beyond the threshold and ridge error smooth.

relationships.display_finding: The peak lay entirely in the variance term while fluctuation-free risk remained smooth, and ridge variance had an additional bump at p=d.
